strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear core insight about decoupling structure from content in multimodal table alignment; comprehensive experimental evaluation across 21 diverse tasks and multiple LVLM architectures with both in-domain and out-of-domain settings

Significant data efficiency: achieves comparable or superior performance to baselines using 97K-150K samples with only 10K training images, with particularly strong out-of-domain generalization (20-30% improvements on OOD benchmarks)

Thorough experimental analysis including understanding-reasoning correlation, performance across varying table layouts, ablations validating each component, and token efficiency analysis; detailed appendices support reproducibility
Consistent improvements across model scales and task types; honest discussion of limitations without attempting to hide trade-offs such as inference latency and token overhead
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: structure anonymization, global/local content alignment, and three-stage reasoning follow straightforward applications of existing techniques; primarily an engineering combination rather than algorithmic innovation

Efficiency claims overclaimed in title and throughout: Table-GLS requires ~2x tokens compared to CoT (492 vs 240), multi-stage reasoning increases inference latency, and 'lightweight' characterization is misleading given computational overhead

Baseline comparisons not entirely fair: optimized LVLM results sourced from different papers with different setups (not directly comparable); GPT-4o-mini uses zero-shot while our method uses alignment; missing comparisons with other structure-aware multimodal or disentanglement approaches

Insufficient analysis of learned representations and error propagation: no validation of model's self-assessment accuracy in plan verification (Eq. 6); unclear whether OOD improvements reflect true structural understanding vs. better pattern matching; failure modes and systematic investigation of struggles absent

DISCO data construction requires manual structured descriptions with subjective complexity assignments; approach to extremely irregular, nested, or non-rectangular tables not explored; automatic extraction accuracy not validated

Statistical rigor lacking: no confidence intervals or significance tests; high variance in some results; several improvements are modest (few percentage points); incremental rather than transformative gains on many tasks
Limited failure case analysis: single positive case study shown; no investigation of task types where method systematically fails; no analysis of whether simpler approaches might suffice

strengths: Novel disentangled structure-content alignment approach that explicitly separates structural learning from semantic grounding, achieving better generalization to unseen table layouts
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 21 tasks and benchmarks with multiple model architectures and scales, including strong OOD generalization results
Practical data efficiency: achieves competitive results with 10K images for alignment compared to 20.6K-82K in prior work, without external tools or additional fine-tuning
Inference-only Table-GLS framework that is lightweight and interpretable, performing structured global-to-local reasoning without additional training

Thorough experimental rigor: detailed ablations validating each component, analysis of table layout impact, correlation analysis between understanding and reasoning, and evaluation on non-tabular tasks to assess transfer
Clear presentation with well-motivated problem statement, detailed methodology description, comprehensive appendices, and honest limitations discussion
weaknesses: Structure-content separation via anonymization may be incomplete—visual layout patterns, table dimensions, and header structures could still implicitly encode content cues; no ablation on alternative anonymization strategies
Prompt engineering sensitivity not addressed—Table-GLS relies heavily on carefully designed prompts but no ablation studies or comparisons with alternative prompt strategies are provided

Incomplete error analysis for Table-GLS: limited characterization of error propagation across stages, and self-refinement (SSE) surprisingly helps on some tasks but hurts on others without clear explanation
Experimental comparison with Textual-All (97K samples) vs. DISCO (10K samples) conflates data quantity with alignment strategy; makes isolating the disentanglement contribution difficult
Significant gap to fully supervised approaches remains: HIPPO achieves 64.63% vs. 58.12% for DISCO+Table-GLS on average reasoning tasks (Qwen3-VL-8B), despite using more training data
Token efficiency tradeoffs underexplored: Table-GLS generates ~2× more tokens than direct answering, with latency implications not thoroughly discussed despite claimed efficiency benefits
Statistical rigor concerns: no error bars, confidence intervals, significance tests, or multiple random seeds reported; makes it unclear if improvements are statistically meaningful

Generalization scope limited: all evaluation within MMTab ecosystem; unclear how approach generalizes to non-English tables, extremely wide tables, complex nested headers, or tables in different document formats
Limited technical ablations on key design choices: no analysis of local content alignment sampling strategy, loss weighting schemes, or sensitivity to the number of alignment samples

strengths: Well-motivated approach addressing practical limitations of table reasoning with LVLMs, eliminating need for expensive supervision or external tools
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 21 diverse benchmarks with consistent improvements, particularly strong on OOD tasks demonstrating good generalization
Achieves competitive performance with only 10K aligned images versus 97K for some baselines, showing data efficiency
Thorough ablation studies and additional analyses (layout impact, understanding-reasoning correlation, token efficiency, prompt sensitivity) demonstrating solid experimental methodology
Practical utility: No external tools required, improvements on general reasoning tasks (Table 5) suggest broader applicability beyond tables
Good reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters, prompts, implementation details provided with commitment to release code
Clear presentation with effective figures and informative case study illustrating the framework's benefits
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: disentangling structure from content is intuitive but not fundamentally novel; structure alignment using placeholder tokens is quite basic lacking theoretical justification

Moderate empirical improvements on many benchmarks (often 2-5%); on some tasks like HiTab direct improvement is marginal or negative; compared to heavily optimized methods (Table-R1, HIPPO), gains are marginal or absent

Self-correction mechanism reliability concern: human evaluation shows only 72-80% success rate for revision step (Table 7), yet this step is critical for robustness; counterintuitive result that removing SSE improves HiTab performance lacks explanation

Data/structure dependencies: method requires structured representations (HTML/Markdown/LaTeX) and still needs 10K aligned images; acknowledged vulnerability to extremely irregular tables significantly limits applicability

Experimental design issues: fairness concerns with comparing against Textual (97K) using different data amounts; OOD evaluation sets are small (250 samples each) without statistical significance testing; ablations mix DISCO and Table-GLS effects
Increased inference latency: 12-15 seconds per sample (Table 8) and ~512 average tokens (2x CoT) limit applicability to latency-sensitive scenarios
Limited analysis of failure modes: single case study, no systematic error analysis, counterintuitive ablation results unexplained, only brief discussion of when approach fails
Scope limitation: focus exclusively on table-centric reasoning; acknowledged generalization to broader structured reasoning problems remains unclear

strengths: Comprehensive evaluation across 21 table understanding and reasoning tasks with extensive ablations, prompt sensitivity analysis, and multiple perspectives (understanding-reasoning correlation, layout robustness, token efficiency)

Strong data efficiency: achieves comparable/superior performance with only 10K alignment images versus 97K baseline images, with particularly impressive OOD generalization demonstrating genuine structure understanding

Well-motivated framework combining intuitive disentangled structure-content alignment with practical multi-stage reasoning; clear presentation with effective visualizations and reproducible implementation details

Practical approach avoiding expensive SFT/RL and external tools while maintaining competitive or superior performance, with reasonable inference latency (14.89s) and demonstrated transferability to non-tabular tasks

Thorough technical execution with sound methodology: proper ablations (DISCO w/o TL, Table-GLS -GSE/-SSE), transparency in data construction and hyperparameters, evaluation across multiple model architectures
weaknesses: Limited novelty: DISCO is fundamentally a data construction strategy with standard alignment losses; Table-GLS is multi-stage prompt engineering. Neither component introduces significant methodological innovation beyond straightforward application of existing techniques

Modest improvements on several key benchmarks (WTQ: 57.11% vs 49.47%, HiTab: 27.35% vs 35.47%, TAT-QA: 40.54% vs 36.01%) and diminished advantages versus heavily optimized baselines (Table-R1, HIPPO), raising questions about true contribution magnitude

Misleading 'no fine-tuning' claim: DISCO requires LoRA-based fine-tuning on 10K annotated images; Table-GLS success depends critically on hand-crafted prompts. The distinction is semantic rather than substantive

Methodological gaps including: no statistical significance testing despite small improvements; self-correction mechanism only works 78-80% of cases with explicit verification not helping (Table 7); only 50 instances manually evaluated for revision success

Incomplete analysis of design choices: surprising result that removing SSE slightly improves HiTab (Table 2) mentioned but not explained; limited failure case discussion; insufficient investigation of why disentanglement helps beyond intuitive motivation

Structure alignment depends on table availability in HTML/Markdown/LaTeX formats; method cannot handle extremely irregular or implicitly-encoded table structures as acknowledged but not deeply addressed

Baseline comparisons use results from original papers rather than controlled re-implementation; token efficiency claims overstated (512 tokens for Table-GLS vs 190 for CoT) despite reasonable absolute latency
